title: Two-body control of noiseless subsystems with mixed $SU(3)$ representations lifts teleportation above the classical fidelity limit
authors: Otavio A. D. Molitor, Sergii Strelchuk, Michał Studziński
abstract: Collective noise can leave degrees of freedom unaffected, allowing them to store quantum information. Processing this information also requires physically available logical gates. We consider $r$ fundamental qutrits transforming under $U\in SU(3)$ and $s$ dual qutrits transforming under its complex conjugate $\overline U$, with collective action $R_{r,s}(U)=U^{\otimes r}\otimes\overline U^{\otimes s}$. Using the image of the walled Brauer algebra and Lie-algebra arguments, we show that adjacent exchanges within each qutrit type and one singlet-projector interaction between the two types generate any independently chosen family of special unitary gates on the noiseless subsystems by a finite pulse sequence, for every $r,s\geq1$. This establishes semi-universality of this system. We illustrate the result with a numerically optimised sequence of 24 pulses for three fundamental qutrits and one dual qutrit. We then use the encoding and available logical corrections for qutrit teleportation under correlated Weyl noise. Under explicit assumptions on channel composition and which trials are retained, and allowing for baseline implementation errors, we identify noise ranges in which encoded teleportation exceeds the classical fidelity bound of $1/2$, while the unencoded teleportation channel is entanglement breaking. We analyse fidelity on accepted trials separately from the transmission costs of the additional physical qutrits.
summary: This paper proves that by utilizing two-body interactions on qutrits encoded in noiseless subsystems, one can achieve full logical control over the encoded quantum information. This capability is then applied to quantum teleportation, showing that the encoded protocol can maintain a fidelity above the classical limit, even when the unencoded channel fails to transmit entanglement.
main_problem: To demonstrate that two-body control over noiseless subsystems encoded in mixed SU(3) representations can enable quantum teleportation fidelity to surpass the classical limit.
main_result: The system achieves semi-universality in logical gate control, and under specific noise conditions, the encoded teleportation fidelity exceeds the classical bound of 1/2 while the unencoded channel is entanglement breaking.
method: The analysis uses Lie-algebra arguments and the structure of the walled Brauer algebra to prove the existence of finite pulse sequences implementing arbitrary logical gates.
model_or_system: The system involves $r$ fundamental qutrits transforming under $U \in SU(3)$ and $s$ dual qutrits under $\overline{U}$. Information is encoded in noiseless subsystems derived from the global Hilbert space $H_{r,s}$.
key_observables: Teleportation fidelity ($F$), entanglement status, and the deviation measure $\varepsilon_\diamond$ from the identity channel.
important_parameters: The number of fundamental ($r$) and dual ($s$) qutrits, and the specific noise parameters defining the Weyl mixture.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on explicit assumptions regarding channel composition, which trials are retained, and accounts for baseline implementation errors.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the analysis compares resources and fidelity bounds for unencoded versus encoded protocols.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical model and the semi-universality of logical gate control using two-body interactions, to applying this framework to analyze and bound the fidelity of quantum teleportation under correlated Weyl noise.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, mathematically rigorous demonstration of how structured noise environments and specific physical interactions (two-body gates) can be harnessed to protect and enhance quantum communication protocols beyond classical limits.

FIG. 1. Recovery of entanglement transmission through en- coding. In the darker interval [3/4, 55/64), the unencoded tele- portation channel is entanglement breaking, while the encoded channel exceeds the classical fidelity bound and can preserve entanglement. The curves use F (0) u = 29/30, F (0) enc = 13/15, and µ = 0.20. The lighter shading begins at 14/19, where the unencoded fidelity reaches 1/2. Fidelities are averaged over accepted trials under the assumptions of Sec. IV C.
